title: Om Is All This
meter: Prose (the Upaniṣad mantras have no meter)
meterNote: The mantras of the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad are prose, not verse, so there is no meter to scan. Their rhythm comes from the chant. Notice how this mantra uses pāda and mātrā, the same two words the meter scanner is built on.
iast: om ity etad akṣaram idaṃ sarvaṃ tasyopavyākhyānaṃ
bhūtaṃ bhavad bhaviṣyad iti sarvam oṅkāra eva |
yac cānyat trikālātītaṃ tad apy oṅkāra eva ||
translation: Om: this syllable is all this. Here is its explanation: the past, the present and the future, all of it is Om alone. And whatever else lies beyond the three times, that too is Om.
translation_hi: ॐ: यह अक्षर ही यह सब कुछ है। उसकी व्याख्या यह है: भूत, वर्तमान और भविष्य, यह सब ओंकार ही है। और जो कुछ तीनों कालों से परे है, वह भी ओंकार ही है।

words.note: iti marks the word as a quotation.
a + kṣara (perishing): a syllable is 'what does not decay'.
Future participle: 'what will be'. Hindi भविष्य.

grammar: One root, three times: √भू gives भूत (past), भवत् (present) and भविष्यत् (future). Hindi still uses भूतकाल and भविष्यकाल.
Akṣara: 'syllable' and 'imperishable' at once. The Upaniṣad means both.
Guṇa sandhi: तस्य + उप → तस्योप, like तस्योपरि in the peacock verse.
